title: Stuffed Pepper with Rice and Meat

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed pepper with rice and meat is a classic dish of Slavic cuisine. Sweet or hot bell peppers are filled with a mixture of boiled rice, ground meat (usually beef or pork), onion, carrot and spices, then baked until tender. The dish combines aromatic meat, fluffy rice and the mild sweetness of the pepper.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stuffed pepper appeared in Russia in the 19th century as a local adaptation of the Turkish dolma.
Traditional recipes often add tomato paste or sauce to the filling for extra juiciness.
Peppers are sometimes blanched before stuffing to make them easier to open.
Different Russian regions use different meats: Siberia often adds venison, the Volga region prefers pork.
The dish is commonly served with sour cream or a tomato‑based sauce.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: The meat in the filling provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice supplies slowly digestible carbs, helping maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Peppers are high in vitamin C, while the meat and rice contribute iron, zinc and B‑vitamins.

items.title: Low added sugar
items.content: The dish contains no added sugars, making it suitable for moderate‑sugar diets.

items.title: Fiber content
items.content: Both pepper and rice add dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to bell peppers, gluten (if a sauce is used) or certain meats.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared sauces or salty seasonings can raise the sodium content of the dish.

items.title: Thorough cooking required
items.content: Meat must be fully cooked to avoid food‑borne illness.

items.title: Dietary restrictions
items.content: People on gluten‑free diets should check sauce ingredients and use gluten‑free spices.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stuffed pepper hot, often alongside mashed potatoes, a fresh salad or a dollop of sour cream. It can be eaten straight from the baking dish or the filling can be lifted with a fork. Leftovers store well in the refrigerator and reheat in the oven or microwave.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the dish to room temperature, then place it in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C before serving.
